tagline: Chicago to Oatman on what is left of the Mother Road.
intro: Out of Chicago the old road runs southwest across Illinois, by the Gemini Giant at Wilmington and the Cozy Dog Drive In at Springfield, to the Mississippi. The byway takes it up again in Oklahoma for some 400 miles, Quapaw to Texola, then crosses New Mexico's eastern prairie, past restored neon and adobe villages, and runs through Arizona to the Black Mountains.

Route 66 was retired in 1985, replaced piece by piece by interstates, and what survives weaves in and out of them. New Mexico advises carrying maps, since the twists and dead ends can leave even well-oriented travelers slightly dazzled.

moments.title: Chain of Rocks Bridge
moments.text: The 1929 bridge takes a 22-degree bend halfway across the Mississippi, forced on it by a water intake and weak bedrock, and now carries only walkers and bicycles.

moments.title: Blue Whale of Catoosa
moments.text: Hugh Davis built the whale of iron and concrete as a 1972 anniversary surprise for his wife, who collected whale figurines. Swimming in its pond is no longer allowed.

moments.title: Oatman
moments.text: A 1915 gold camp that passed 3,500 people in a year and was bypassed in 1953. Wild burros walk the street, and federal officials call it a town basically all about burros.

practical: Near Oatman the old road crosses Sitgreaves Pass in the Black Mountains on hairpin curves and steep grades.
